_provenance: Structure transcribed from a LIVE capture on 2026-08-28 (see architecture/data.md §get_add_to_playlist): POST /youtubei/v1/playlist/get_add_to_playlist {videoIds:[id]} against a 256-playlist brand account, 230 KB, ~180 ms, 200 rows. Ids and titles are replaced; the shape, key names and enum values are verbatim. This REPLACES add-to-playlist-panel-synthetic.json, which encoded a guessed `selected: true` flag on a bare playlists[] array — a shape the live capture disproved. The renderer is `playlistAddToOptionRenderer` and membership is the `containsSelectedVideos` enum, never a boolean. Rows are nested two levels deeper than the old guess, which is exactly why parsing must walk rather than index.
_note: The live response carries 200 such rows and NO continuation token. That 200 is a hard server cap — the same 200 ids come back for every videoId — so any playlist absent from this list is UNKNOWN, not absent-from. YouTube's own Save popover is built from the same 200 and is equally blind past it.
